rationale: C23 is the strongest candidate because it concerns the National Guard within the National Military Establishment and directs the Secretary of Defense to act and report to the President. But its operative program—organizing and training reserve components—is materially different from the child's delegation of presidential supervision over the District of Columbia National Guard and its appointment-recommendation procedure. C07 shares references to action on behalf of the President and recommendations involving the Secretary of Defense, while C13 contains delegation machinery, but neither supplies the child's distinctive two-part administrative structure. The similarities are topical or routine rather than evidence of a reusable drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense is authorized and directed to supervise and control, on behalf of the President
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense, and the head of each department in the national Military Establishment, shall proceed without delay
shared_material.explanation: C23 uses the same principal official in an armed-forces directive, but assigns a different substantive function and does not reproduce the child's supervision-and-control delegation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense shall at such times as may be appropriate submit to the President recommendations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense shall within 60 days after the date of this order submit to the President a report
shared_material.explanation: C23 has a superficially parallel reporting provision, but a report on reserve organization is not the same administrative machinery as recommendations concerning appointments.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Committee is authorized on behalf of the President to examine into the rules, procedures and practices of the armed services
shared_material.explanation: C07 shares this phrase and a military-administration setting, but the phrase supports a committee investigation rather than presidential supervision of the District of Columbia National Guard.
